results.controlIntent: a. Identify and document [Assignment: organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation]; and b. Define system access authorizations to support separation of duties.

judgment.rationale:
The IAM execution role attached to the churn-predictor-endpoint (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic) grants two wildcard policies that fundamentally violate Separation of Duties (AC-5):

1. **SageMakerFull** (`sagemaker:*` on `*`): The inference endpoint's execution role has full SageMaker permissions. This means the same role that serves predictions can also create/delete models, launch training jobs, modify endpoints, and perform administrative actions. These are distinct duties (inference vs. training vs. administration) that must be separated under AC-5.

2. **OverlyBroadS3** (`s3:*` on `*`): The inference role has unrestricted S3 access including write permissions to all buckets. An inference endpoint should only need read access to model artifacts — not write access to training data buckets or cross-account S3 resources. This collapses the data-scientist/trainer duty and the inference-operator duty into one role.

AC-5 requires (a) identifying and documenting duties requiring separation, and (b) defining access authorizations to enforce that separation. Neither requirement is met: there is no evidence of duty decomposition, and the access authorizations actively consolidate conflicting duties (training, deployment, inference, administration) into a single generic role. The role name "SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic" further suggests no role-per-function design was applied.
gaps: No documentation of defined duties requiring separation (e.g., a RACI matrix or access control policy document) was available for review.
No evidence of separate roles for training, deployment, and inference functions — only the single endpoint execution role was retrievable.
Human attestation would be needed to confirm whether compensating controls (e.g., SCPs, permission boundaries, or manual approval workflows) exist outside the IAM role configuration.

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
